outline_section.section_title: Introduction to Using Derivatives to Transform Piecewise Linear Signals
outline_section.learning_goal: Introduce the section-level workflow: compute $x'(t)$ from a piecewise-linear $x(t)$, map derivative terms with one-sided derivative Laplace rules, and solve algebraically for $X(s)$.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A compact figure with three time-domain sketches: causal ramp, shifted ramp, finite ramp ending at a breakpoint. Emphasize slope regions, breakpoint instants, and corresponding derivative support.
visual_elements: vertical impulse glyphs at derivative singularities
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use one figure only to build the visual schema: each example will reuse this motif through symbolic text in follow-up steps.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Show learners how to execute the exact operational chain: differentiate the selected piecewise-linear signal, apply the appropriate derivative-domain identity, then isolate $X(s)$.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Start from $x(t)=t\,u(t)$, where $x'(t)=u(t)$ and $x(0^-)=0$, then map to $X(s)$ directly.
paragraph_plan: Name the two core transforms to use repeatedly: $\mathcal{L}\{x'(t)\}=sX(s)-x(0^-)$ and time-shifted versions of unit-step / impulse pairs.
Explain how a piecewise-linear signal becomes a sum of ramp terms and how its derivative becomes constant steps plus impulses at breakpoints.
Show the role of one-sided initial value terms in isolating $X(s)$ and prevent the common shortcut of copying bilateral formulas.
Use a single sketch to connect each slope region and breakpoint to its transformed term before moving to worked examples.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep the tutorial conceptual and compact. Set a reusable move template: identify derivative term types, write transforms term-by-term, and solve for $X(s)$. Avoid introducing additional formulas not needed in examples.
